text:
michael: Heads up  vendor DataForge LLC sent invoice and asked us to gross-up for US withholding. They attached a W-9 but their payment instructions show an Irish bank (IBAN). They say they're a US LLC taxed as a disregarded entity but routing via EU. Thoughts?

sarah: That sounds messy. If they provided a valid W-9 and claim US tax residency then no 30% withholding should apply. But the bank location shouldn't change withholding. Do we have their EIN on the W-9?

michael: W-9 fields: Name: DataForge LLC; TIN/EIN: 12-3456789; Address: 201 Market St, San Francisco, CA. Bank: Bank of Dublin, IBAN IE29ABCD...

diego: Two operational points: 1) AP needs a matching W-9 on file before we can pay net; 2) If they ask for gross-up, that implies they expect us to bear withholding taxes. We don't gross-up for domestic US vendors. We only do gross-up rarely and only with pre-approved contracts.

tax-ops: Confirming tax perspective: If vendor is US resident (W-9 + EIN), no US withholding. The routing through an EU bank is likely their treasury arrangement and doesn't create withholding obligations for us. If they were foreign (W-8), then 30% could apply absent treaty and documentation. So request clarification and proof of EIN match (EIN validation or copy of SS-4), and verify name on bank account for sanctions/AML.

michael: Vendor insists their bank charges an "outgoing tax" and asks Redwood to gross-up net to cover it. Any precedent?

sarah: We've had one prior case where a payment processor levied an outbound fee; we didn't gross-up. We reimbursed fees only when contract specified. Recommend denial unless contract says otherwise.

diego: AP note: We can pay via our usual wire and indicate payment instructions. If they want a different method to avoid bank fees, suggest ACH to US bank or Stripe payout. Offer to pay net and provide a payment remittance that shows W-9 on file.

ap-bot: (automated) Vendor DataForge LLC onboarding status: Tax doc W-9 received. Payment terms: NET30. Bank details unverified.

michael: I'll reply to vendor: "We have your W-9 on file showing US tax residency; Redwood does not gross-up for external bank charges. Please provide EIN confirmation if different, or request alternative payout method. If you require gross-up per an existing contract clause, escalate with contract reference." I'll CC tax-ops and legal.

tax-ops: Good. If they push that funds sent via Ireland trigger source-country taxes, ask them to provide legal basis. We can re-evaluate with counsel but default is no gross-up.

sarah: Also ask vendor to confirm beneficiary name matches registered name to avoid payment holds.

michael: Sending response now. Closing thread after vendor reply.
